artifacts.summary: Nine-phase, 15-hour plan to convert 36 proof bodies to applyRule.eq_N rewrites behind named wrappers, with before/after heartbeat evidence and a per-rule exclusion fallback.

memory_candidates.content: Lean 4 cost anti-pattern with measured attribution: a proof body shaped as `unfold <bigMatchDef> at h` followed by `repeat' split at h` and then `all_goals (try simp_all only [...])` is pathologically expensive, and the cost is in simp, not in the unfold. Profiled on a 36-arm match definition (FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/Verified/Termination/SubformulaProperty.lean, 36 such bodies): `lake env lean -Dprofiler=true -Dprofiler.threshold=200` attributed 14,987.6s to simp across 1348 calls (99.2 percent) against 108s for ALL tactic execution combined (0.7 percent) and 1.55s for imports. The splitter leaves ~37 goals, each carrying both the unfolded definition and the accumulated guard hypotheses, and simp_all rewrites that whole context once per goal. The remedy is the per-arm equation lemmas Lean already generates for any match-defined function (`f.eq_1 ... f.eq_N` plus a catch-all `f.eq_<N+1>` whose hypotheses are `... -> False` guards): rewriting with the right `eq_N` replaces the cascade with a two-or-three-goal proof. Measured A/B: 882,487 -> 760 heartbeats; 2,084,589 -> 146. Two discipline notes: `#count_heartbeats` requires `set_option Elab.async false` or every count reads ~30 (the proof elaborates on another thread), and `eq_N` numbering is generator-assigned and tracks arm order, so downstream proofs should name a wrapper theorem per arm rather than the raw `eq_N`. Restructuring the definition into per-arm sub-definitions is the obvious-looking fix and is wrong: the dispatch cost it removes is inside the sub-1-percent tactic-execution slice.
